title: The Trumpeter Taken Prisoner
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Trumpeter marched into battle in the van of the army and put courage into his comrades by his warlike tunes. Being captured by the enemy, he begged for his life, and said, "Do not put me to death; I have killed no one: indeed, I have no weapons, but carry with me only my trumpet here." But his captors replied, "That is only the more reason why we should take your life; for, though you do not fight yourself, you stir up others to do so."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did the Trumpeter march into battle?
options: At the rear of the army
In the van of the army
Alongside the cavalry only
Behind the supply wagons

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Trumpeter put courage into his comrades?
options: By fighting alongside them with a sword
By his warlike tunes
By shouting orders at them
By carrying their banner into battle

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Trumpeter do after being captured by the enemy?
options: He offered to join their side
He begged for his life
He tried to escape immediately
He refused to speak to his captors

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what reason does the Trumpeter give for sparing his life?
options: He has a family waiting for him at home
He has killed no one and carries no weapons but his trumpet
He was forced into the army against his will
He knows valuable information about the enemy

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what do the captors say is the reason they should take the Trumpeter's life?
options: He deceived them about his identity
He stirs up others to fight, even though he does not fight himself
He refused to surrender his trumpet
He had previously fought against them directly

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "van" mean in "marched into battle in the van of the army"?
options: A type of covered wagon
The rear guard of an army
The front, leading position of a force
A reserve unit kept out of battle

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why do the captors reject the Trumpeter's defense that he carries no weapons?
options: They believe he is lying about being unarmed
They value his trumpet as a war prize
They see his music as a weapon that rouses others to fight, even without a sword in his hand
They think all musicians should be spared regardless

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Trumpets should never be used on the battlefield
One who incites others to violence bears responsibility even without striking a blow himself
Soldiers who carry no weapons are always spared by their captors
Music has no real influence on the outcome of a battle

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Trumpeter say he carries with him?
options: A shield and a spear
Only his trumpet
A sword he never used
Supplies for the army

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who captured the Trumpeter?
options: Deserters from his own army
The enemy
A band of robbers
His own commanding officer

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what exact words do the captors use to justify killing the Trumpeter?
options: "You are far too dangerous to release"
"That is only the more reason why we should take your life; for, though you do not fight yourself, you stir up others to do so"
"Your trumpet has caused us great losses"
"We cannot trust the word of a musician"

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "stir up" mean in "you stir up others to do so"?
options: Confuse or mislead
Rouse or provoke into action
Quietly organize in secret
Physically move from place to place

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what assumption does the Trumpeter make about how guilt in war should be judged?
options: He assumes that only those who physically fight and kill are guilty
He assumes that anyone captured is automatically guilty
He assumes that musicians are exempt from all rules of war
He assumes that his captors will not believe anything he says

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A captured Trumpeter argues he is innocent because he carries no weapons, but his captors say his music makes him just as responsible as a fighter
A Trumpeter is captured and immediately released as harmless
A Trumpeter switches sides and joins his captors' army
A Trumpeter defeats his captors using only his trumpet
